record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Strict proof of half-width finger selection
record.original_question: Can one give a strict proof, for zero-surface-tension Saffman-Taylor channel growth in the pole-solution formulation, that the exclusion of finite-time-singular initial pole configurations together with continual introduction of new poles selects a single finger of half the channel width as the privileged or most probable asymptotic state?

evidence.quote: It does not mean, nevertheless, that privileged role of "finger" with thickness 1/2 cannot be proved in the case of surface tension absence, but means only that such the proof are not given in [3]. Let us try to give these correct arguments here.
Source of new poles results to the drift of finger thickness, but this thickness drift is closed to the most probable and average size equal to 1/2!
These given arguments are not, certainly, the strict proof, but only specifies a way to it. The inquisitive reader is invited to make and publish it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional Saffman–Taylor problem of Hele-Shaw channel flow with zero surface tension. The channel has width 1, and a less viscous fluid displaces a more viscous fluid satisfying Darcy's law, so that the interface evolves by Laplacian growth (the normal velocity of the interface equals the normal derivative of a harmonic pressure field, with constant pressure on the interface). Using a conformal map from the exterior of the unit disk to the fluid domain, the dynamics admit a pole-decomposition formulation: the conformal map has the form of a sum of logarithmic poles whose positions in the complex plane evolve according to an autonomous system of ODEs. New poles may be continually introduced into the configuration during the evolution.

Adopt the following regularization rule (without invoking surface tension): at every time, exclude any pole configuration (whether initial or newly introduced) that would lead to a finite-time singularity (a cusp on the moving interface). With this rule in force, and allowing continual introduction of new admissible poles:

Provide a rigorous mathematical proof that the asymptotic state (as t → ∞) of this dynamics is, in the privileged or "most probable" sense (e.g., almost surely under a reasonable measure on admissible pole insertions, or as the unique attractor of the regularized dynamics), a single Saffman–Taylor finger occupying exactly one half of the channel width. Equivalently, prove that the relative finger width λ(t) converges to 1/2 under the pole-dynamics formulation with the above non-surface-tension regularization.
artifact.status_search_result: Several works (Mineev-Weinstein, PRL 1998; subsequent Laplacian Growth papers) claim that pole dynamics with regularization (no surface tension) selects a single 1/2-width finger asymptotically and present arguments toward an "exact result." However, this claim was contested by a published Comment (PRL 81, 5950), and the rigor and generality of the proof remain debated. No universally accepted strict proof appears in the literature, so the precise question of a fully rigorous proof of half-width selection in this pole formulation is best classified as unknown/partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Selection of the Saffman-Taylor Finger Width in the Absence of Surface Tension: An Exact Result
status_evidence.snippet: Claims that a generic interface evolves to a single uniformly advancing finger occupying one-half of the channel width, contradicting the belief that surface tension is indispensable.
status_evidence.claim: Argues for 1/2-width selection without surface tension via pole dynamics.
